diagnosis: All four rollouts revealed both PF1 and PF2 and cited them in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy problems. The gate failed solely because check C4 failed in rollouts 0 and 3. In those two rollouts, the model split the two corrected limits from PF2 (audience capacity 180 and sound limit 82 dBA) into separate commitments and did not explicitly name the signed inspection note or PF2 within the commitment text that records the limit changes. In the two passing rollouts (1 and 2), the model combined both corrected limits into a single commitment and either referenced the signed inspection note explicitly (rollout 2: "referencing signed inspection note") or cited the amended permit conditions as the source (rollout 1: "per amended permit conditions"). This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: C4 requires a specific commitment structure—both limits in one commitment with explicit citation of PF2—that the model only sometimes produces naturally.

C4.why: The signed inspection note changes the audience limit from 220 to exactly 180 and the post-9:00 PM sound limit from 90 to exactly 82 dBA, requiring a commitment that records both corrected limits and explicit citation of PF2.
